advice: Propose a guarded n==512 wrapper experiment using the supplied sera_libxsmm_panel32 helper: replace the single sera_libxsmm_512 call with 16 calls for row bands r=0,32,...,480. For each call, zero-initialize parameters[22], set [4]=B, [10]=A+(size_t)r*512, and [16]=C+(size_t)r*512; leave all other fields zero. This removes the full kernel's 128 KiB scratch allocation per 64-row band and its packing of 64 A rows at a time. Each helper call packs a 32-row A panel into 64 KiB, computes its full 512-column band, and stores directly to that band. Keep the non-512 fallback and helper assembly unchanged. Hypothesis: the smaller per-call panel and altered packing/cache working set may improve performance. This is unverified advice; available measurements do not establish a speedup.
risks: Sixteen helper calls each enter and exit SME and pack independently, instead of one full-kernel call with an overall SME entry and exit. The extra transition and call overhead may outweigh any benefit from the smaller scratch panel; buffer size alone does not predict the outcome. Check all 512 output rows are covered once with no overlap, pointer offsets and zeroed parameter fields match the helper ABI, and general sizes plus n<=0 still use the existing fallback. Preserve the BSD notice. Validate full GEMM correctness at tolerance 0.002 under the fixed build, then use fresh repeated paired controls on the block's unchanged power source and settings; keep AC and battery results separate. Do not claim causality from noisy scores or attribute a joint result to this experiment alone.
